title: Hartland fire of 1907, west side of Main St.
description: The fire was discovered around one o’clock on Monday morning on July 15, 1907, in the rear of the W. F. Thornton drug store. Amasa Plummer, who lived next door above the Keith & Plummer store, was awakened by smoke and flames and immediately sounded the alarm. After two rings of the bell and the terrifying midnight cry of “fire.” Those two taps were enough to rouse the neighborhood. Before the firefighters arrived with their apparatus, flames were already soaring skyward behind the drug store. The blaze swept along the west side of Main Street, from the ramp and toll house at the Hartland Bridge to the Tracey building just beyond the current library (which was not affected, as it was built in 1912). Explosions shattered windows on the buildings across the street. In total, twenty-three businesses and twelve family and professional residences were lost.
